flags.quote: Moving your c3-knight to e4 is the strongest move because it saves your e4-knight from capture.
flags.critique: The sentence names two different squares for one knight. It was hanging on c3 under the queen on b3; e4 is where it ran. I cannot trust a coach that cannot keep the piece on the square it started on.

flags.quote: Moving your king to h8 weakens the pawns in front of your king. A better move would have been taking the pawn on c5 with your e4-knight because you fork the white queen and the white d3-bishop and then fork the white queen and the white d3-bishop.
flags.critique: The king stepped into the corner. That does not weaken the pawn shield; the pawns did not move. Nexc5 really does fork queen and bishop, which is the lesson I needed, and then you said the same fork twice like a stuck record.

flags.quote: Taking the rook on d1 with your f2-knight is the strongest move because you come out a bishop ahead.
flags.critique: I took a rook with a knight. That is the exchange, not a bishop. If the recapture nets +2, do not round it to a piece I did not win. I will miscount every trade after this.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on c3 with your e4-knight makes your king easier to attack. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e5.
flags.critique: My king is already castled. Snatching the c3 pawn does not strip its cover. The real question is whether the knight gets stuck and whether ...e5 in the center was the break. King-safety as the headline here is a detector lie.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your king to a3 leaves your pawn hanging to the black queen. A better move would have been moving your pawn to h6 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Yes, a5 hangs to Qd8. Then you recommend h6 to save 'your pawn.' h6 does not defend a5. The better-move clause is a leftover saves-pawn template that does not even point at the hanging pawn you just named.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to g4 gives you a backward pawn. A better move would have been taking the knight on e4 with your d3-bishop because you can likely fork the black king and the black d7-knight and then take a pawn.
flags.critique: g4 is a king-still-in-the-center pawn storm, not a backward-pawn lecture. Bxe4 is the real idea: take the octopus. Inventing a king-and-knight fork and a free pawn after that is SEE fan fiction. I wanted 'take the knight before it kills you.'

flags.quote: Moving your queen to b3 is playable, but moving your queen to c2 would be better.
flags.critique: Black's knight is sitting on c3 with nobody defending it. That is the entire position. You never say 'the knight is hanging.' Qc2 vs Qb3 is a footnote; collecting or firmly attacking the free piece is the class.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h4 is a mistake, but moving your pawn to a5 would be better because you can likely take a knight.
flags.critique: a5 does not take a knight. I stared at d7 and e4 and nothing is en prise to that pawn. The actual lesson is you launched a rook pawn with the king still on e1. 'Likely take a knight' is a dare, not a reason.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e5 is a blunder, but moving your pawn to f5 would be better because it unveils an attack from your queen on the white pawn and then take a pawn.
flags.critique: That last clause is not English: 'and then take a pawn.' A 385-centipawn swing and you cannot say which pawn, or why opening the center with the king on e1 and a knight on e4 explodes. Name the discovered queen hit on the kingside and stop trailing off.

flags.quote: Taking the bishop on c3 with your b-pawn is the strongest move because the bishop was undefended.
flags.critique: I recaptured a checking bishop. Of course it was hanging; I was in check. The reasons already know about doubled and isolated pawns and you hid them. Teach me that I just wrecked my c-structure, not that capturing the checker wins material.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f6 gives you a backward pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e5.
flags.critique: Lichess called this a blunder because I ripped holes around my king, not because some pawn became 'backward.' I do not know which pawn you mean and I do not care. Say the dark squares and the king, then sell ...e5 as the break.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a5 gives you a backward pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to f4.
flags.critique: Fourth time this game a pawn push is 'backward pawn.' f4 kicks the knight on g5. That is a 1200 lesson. Calling a5 a structure crime while the knight sits on g5 is coaching from the wrong file.

flags.quote: Taking the knight on c3 with your b4-bishop is the strongest move because you pin the pawn to the rook.
flags.critique: I took on c3 with check because a3 asked the bishop a question and I doubled White's pawns. A pin of b2 to a1 is a trivia fact after the check. Do not lead with a pin nobody is thinking about while the structure change is the whole Nimzo/Slav idea.

flags.quote: Moving your king to d2 makes your king easier to attack. A better move would have been moving your king to f1 because your king is harder to attack.
flags.critique: Easier to attack versus harder to attack is the same sentence with a hat on. Lichess called this a blunder: the king walked into the center onto a crowded file. Tell me Kf1 tucks away and Kd2 steps into checks, not two king_safer phrases fighting.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your king to b2 leaves your pawn hanging to the black bishop. A better move would have been taking the knight on e4 with your d3-bishop because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: g4 hangs to the c8 bishop; that part is true. Bxe4 does not save g4. If you meant f2 hanging to the knight, you named the wrong attacker two clauses ago. Pick one pawn and make the better move actually defend it.

flags.quote: You are still worse, but moving your h1-rook to d1 puts it where the black f2-knight can take and you lose the exchange. A better move would have been moving your c1-bishop to d2 because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: The played-move half is finally honest: I parked the rook on the forked square. Then Bd2 'saves your pawn from capture' like we are not talking about a rook. If the fix is to meet the fork, say that. Do not change the subject to a pawn.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c5 creates a backward pawn to defend. A better move would have been moving your pawn to a4.
flags.critique: 'Creates a backward pawn to defend' is not a sentence a human says. c5 lets go of the d5 tension, leaves the doubled c3 pawn sick, and hands Black a clamp to undermine. a4 as the improvement needs a reason, not structure jargon.

flags.quote: Moving your f6-knight to e4 is playable, but moving your pawn to b6 would be better because you can likely take a pawn.
flags.critique: ...b6 undermines c5. Say that. 'You can likely take a pawn' is a weasel SEE line: take with what, if White recaptures, which pawn. Ne4 is an outpost; do not bury that under a fake capture.

flags.quote: Taking the pawn on d4 with your e-pawn puts it at risk of attack from the white pawn. A better move would have been moving your pawn to e4 because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: I captured on d4. White's e-pawn can take back. That is called recapturing, not 'putting it at risk of attack from the white pawn.' Lichess called it a blunder; you called it a mistake and then sold ...e4 as king safety. Open files and the g5 knight are the story.

flags.quote: Moving your g5-knight to e4 keeps you winning because it keeps your king safer and it attacks the king directly.
flags.critique: A check does not make my king safer. 'Attacks the king directly' is just the word check wearing a suit. Bxg4 was the extra pawn; lead with the hanging g4 pawn, not two canned king phrases.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to h5 is a blunder, but taking the knight on e4 with your d3-bishop would be better because it keeps your king safer.
flags.critique: Almost 500 centipawns and the punchline is king safety. Bxe4 removes the piece that is eating your position while you still have not castled. 'Keeps your king safer' could be pasted on any move in the file.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to f3 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: You lost 109 centipawns and still said strongest. Matching the engine's top UCI should not override a triple-digit swing. Also 'saves your pawn' without saying f2 was hanging to the knight is the same nameless-pawn disease as Ka3 and Rd1.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to c6 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: No reasons, no Slav, no 'this backs up d5 so you can take back with a pawn.' This is the name of the opening and you gave me a blank strongest-move stamp and 'That's the one.' I learned zero.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to a3 is the strongest move.
flags.critique: The bishop is pinning my knight to the king. a3 asks it to take or leave. Empty copy here is malpractice: this is the one move where 'challenge the pin' would actually stick.

flags.quote: Moving your pawn to e3 is the strongest move because it saves your pawn from capture.
flags.critique: Which pawn? c4 is hanging to ...dxc4, but you never say that, and e3 also opens the bishop and solidifies d4. 'Saves your pawn from capture' is the same clause you later glue onto h6, Bd2, and f3. I am numb to it.

suggestions.title: Name the saved piece on its origin square
suggestions.detail: saves_piece uses namedUnitAt(after, move.to), so a retreat is 'your e4-knight' when the hanging piece was on c3. Pass the from-square (or the hanging-before unit) into the reason. A 1200 notices instantly when the because-clause contradicts the SAN.

suggestions.title: Stop leading with backward-pawn on every pawn push
suggestions.detail: c5, f6, g4, and a5 all got problem_backward_pawn while the real ideas were tension, king holes, taking Ne4, and kicking Ng5. Rank tactics, hanging pieces, and king-shelter damage above structure.backwardPawnsCreated unless the position is a quiet endgame.

suggestions.title: Do not say likely-take unless the capture is on the board next ply
suggestions.detail: Suggested-move copy invented 'likely take a knight' (a5), 'likely take a pawn' (...b6), and 'likely fork king and knight and then take a pawn' (Bxe4). verifyLikelyTactics should require the capture square to be attacked by the suggested piece after one legal ply, not a SEE chain of follow-ups glued with 'and then.'

suggestions.title: Call +200 from rook-for-knight the exchange
suggestions.detail: materialLabel maps 200–249 to 'a bishop', so Nxd1+ became 'a bishop ahead.' If the captured type is a rook and SEE is ~200, emit 'the exchange' (or 'a rook for a knight'). Learners will mis-count trades until this is fixed.

suggestions.title: If a piece is hanging, that is the lesson
suggestions.detail: Qb3 vs Qc2 never mentioned the undefended knight on c3. pickBenefitReasons / pickProblemReasons should promote hanging/capture over empty missed_improvement when the PV collects a free piece. Same for Rd1 walking onto a fork: the better move must talk about the rook, not a nameless pawn.

suggestions.title: Tie the better-move because-clause to the hanging unit you named
suggestions.detail: Ka3: a5 hangs to the queen, but h6 'saves your pawn.' Kb2: g4 hangs to the bishop, but Bxe4 'saves your pawn.' The saves_piece fallback is winning the because-slot. If describePlayedProblem names a hanging unit, the suggested because must defend, recapture, or ignore that same unit, or drop saves_piece.

suggestions.title: Do not concatenate the same fork twice
suggestions.detail: Nexc5 rendered 'fork the white queen and the white d3-bishop and then fork the white queen and the white d3-bishop.' sameFocusPiece / selectBecauseReasons should drop a follow-up that lists the same target set. Cheap, and it reads like a bug to every learner.

suggestions.title: Do not stamp strongest on a 100cp swing
suggestions.detail: classifyPlayedMove returns best whenever UCI matches the engine move, even at 109cp (f3). The comment says 'tiny' MultiPV noise; cap the override at excellentMaxLossCp (20) or goodMaxLossCp (50). 'The strongest move' after a triple-digit drop trains people to ignore the eval bar.

whatWorked: Bb4: pin the knight to the king is the actual idea, said plainly.
Kingside castling: shelter plus rook toward the center, not a blank stamp.
exd4: discovered the c1 bishop onto the g5 knight; rare case of unveils-an-attack landing on the right piece.
Re8+: open file and forces the king to respond.
Kc3: king step that unveils Bc1 onto Ng5 is a real discovered-attack lesson.
Nf2: fork bishop and rook, named both targets.
Qxa5+: skewer on the a-file exposing the a1 rook.
Kb2: discovered rook onto the queen, which is why the king stepped off the skewer.
Qb4+: actually did save the hanging queen.
Qxd4: pin the bishop to the queen plus hanging pawn, both true.
